speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your vision changes, can you tell me if the black spots are stationary or if they move around your field of view? Also, have you noticed any pain in the eye or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and Kaposi's sarcoma, I am concerned about opportunistic infections like cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. REQUEST TEST: Dilated Fundus Examination

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy reveals granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopic findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages are classic for CMV retinitis, especially given your history of AIDS and opportunistic infections. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other potential pathogens, I would like to see any available medical images of the retina. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of painless vision loss with floaters, combined with the characteristic "pizza pie" retinopathy findings, confirms the diagnosis in the context of advanced AIDS. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis
